newsitem.title: UK: BT says eurobond issue driven by MCI merger.
newsitem.headline: BT says eurobond issue driven by MCI merger.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc's $1.0 billion Eurobond launched on Tuesday was driven by its need for funds ahead of its multi-billion trans-Atlantic merger with MCI Communications Corp, group treasurer Andy Longden said.
"We need the money as in the last five to six years we've repaid a considerable amount of debt, (and we also need it for) BT's merger with MCI which we expect to complete by September," he said.
"We have to make a cash payment to MCI shareholders in the region of $2.5 billion in September," he added.
BT will also offer shares to MCI shareholders and the merged group will be called Concert Plc, he said.

Concert wants to provide clients around the globe with local, long distance, international and mobile phone services as well as multi-media, internet-based services and systems integration for business clients.
After the merger the combined firm will be the second largest telecommunications company in the world with around $40.6 billion in revenues.
Tuesday's $1.0 billion five-year deal was hailed a "blow-out" by both lead managers -- Merrill Lynch and SBC Warburg -- and syndicate officials at rival banks.
The deal was priced to yield 15 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, and was trading at 14.5 b.p. over on the bid at 1530 GMT.
"We're delighted by the response from the market," Longden told Reuters. "The five-year maturity fitted well with our maturity profile and with the demand in the market," he added.
"We remain on watch for attractive funding opportunities but we have no current plans. We regularly monitor the markets and look at all currencies and maturities."
He denied "mischievous rumours" that BT were about to follow the dollar deal with a sterling offering.
"We have a high regard for our investor base and we seek to protect it in order to preserve our ability to come back to the market," Longden said.
"We took a great deal of trouble and time over the dollar deal to ensure it will be a success," he said.
The rarity of BT paper also boosted demand. BT last tapped the dollar sector in July 1994.
The syndicate manager at Merrill Lynch said there had been a "phenomenal response" to the deal.
"BT is a very special name and investors have jumped all over it...they love telecom companies and these types of bonds are like gold dust," he said.
With regards to the corporate's ratings, Longden said BT would remain a very attractive name in the debt markets despite losing its AAA credit rating.
Moody's Investors Service downgraded BT to AA1 from AAA and Standard & Poor's Corp has put its AAA rating for BT's long-term debt under review for possible downgrade.
Dealers on Tuesday said the credit rating was less relevant to the transaction than BT's future earning potential following the merger with MCI.
